subject: Private offer renewal — commit top-up clarification and acceptance path
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@heliotech.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private offer renewal — commit top-up clarification and acceptance path

Hi Aisha,

Thanks again for the conversation yesterday. Per our discussion, HelioTech is looking to renew the marketplace private offer for the next 12 months and add a capacity top-up (~40% over current committed usage) with a staged billing plan. Before we generate the amended PO, I need to confirm two operational points so we align the acceptance and invoicing windows: 

1) Usage buckets: do you want the top-up to be applied as a permanent increase to the committed units (billing baseline), or treated as a separate tranche that only triggers after the baseline is consumed? If tranche, which sequence do you prefer — monthly pro-rata vs quarterly catch-up?

2) Acceptance tests: the existing acceptance window in your current private offer was 14 days for the first tranche. Will you accept the same conditions for the top-up, or should we add an interim 7-day smoke-test to speed activation?

We can support either approach but need the procurement preference so the billing and SLA notes in the DocuSign + AWS PO match. I attached the signed amendment we discussed (signed_amendment_v2.pdf) and a first-pass billing tranche spreadsheet.

Short next steps I propose: 
- You confirm tranche vs baseline behavior and acceptance window by EOD tomorrow.
- We issue updated PO + DocuSign for signatures once procurement confirms.

Thanks — looping Marissa and Laura for any billing/legal flags.

Best,
Diego
Senior Sales Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachment: signed_amendment_v2.pdf (application/pdf)
Attachment: proposed-billing-tranches.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Aisha Thomas <aisha.thomas@heliotech.io>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 Oct 2028 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private offer renewal — commit top-up clarification and acceptance path

Diego,

Thanks for the clear summary. Procurement prefers to keep the baseline committed units intact and have the top-up handled as a separate tranche that we pay for only if the baseline is exhausted. Preference is quarterly catch-up rather than monthly churn — simpler for our finance team.

For acceptance, we can do a 7-day smoke-test on the first tranche and then revert to a 14-day window for subsequent tranches. The faster smoke-test helps us kick off onboarding earlier.

I'm including procurement@heliotech.io to coordinate PO timing. We'll aim to get an internal approval by next Wednesday.

—Aisha
Aisha Thomas
Head of Product Ops, HelioTech

Perfect — quarterly catch-up and 7-day smoke for the first tranche is doable.

Aisha / procurement team: to make the DocuSign + AWS PO clean on your side we'll do the following: 
- Create the top-up as a separate tranche line item on the private offer (Tranche B) with quarterly catch-up billing.
- Smoke acceptance for Tranche B will be a 7-calendar-day window that starts on first activation.
- SLA & credits: we will keep the same SLO banding for the baseline and apply a pro-rated SLA credit for Tranche B for any partial-month downtime in the first quarter.

Karthik / Marissa: two asks for your teams: 
1) Can legal provide a one-page redline with the minimum change set we need to include in the DocuSign so HelioTech procurement can sign without full legal review? (HelioTech is sensitive to any new data residency clauses right now.)
2) Billing: please produce an updated quote showing baseline vs tranche costs and the quarterly billing schedule so Aisha can circulate to finance. I've attached the proposed-billing-tranches.xlsx for reference.

Aisha — once we have the one-pager and updated quote I will push the DocuSign and the AWS PO draft (we'll provision AWS PO ID in the header so their procurement can reference it). If procurement can aim for a PO by next Wednesday that keeps us on the timeline for an Oct 20 activation.

Diego

Diego — thanks for the summary. Quick legal/billing notes: 

1) Legal: I attached a short redline (redlines_markup.docx) that limits changes to the billing appendix and the acceptance window. We explicitly do NOT add any new data residency terms; call that out in the contract preface so HelioTech's legal can skip a full round.

2) Billing: Marissa, can you generate a per-quarter quote that shows: baseline committed units (current price), Tranche B quarterly usage tiers with per-unit rates, and an example calculation for a 40% top-up realized across Q1? The customer asked for a modeled example in absolute dollars for finance. Please also include the invoice schedule we discussed (quarterly, with a 14-day payment term).

3) Ops: We will include AWS PO ID placeholder (AWS-PO-987654) in the DocuSign so procurement can reference it when they issue their internal PO. Diego — I recommend including the HubSpot link in the DocuSign email so their procurement approver has the deal context.

I'll keep the redline tight and backward compatible.

Karthik Iyer
Head of Legal, Redwood Inference
